text.p: Mark Ealham celebrated his selection for this week's Texaco Trophy one-day matches against Australia with a match-winning all-round performance for Kent in the Sunday League.
Ealham, named in England's 15-man squad earlier in the day, hit a whirlwind 61 after coming in at number six to help Kent to 238 for nine against Glamorgan.
Then he polished off the tail with five wickets at the death, clean bowling four of them just when the Welshmen threatened after a bold 65 from Adrian Dale only to fall eight runs short.
It was Kent's third victory and they are joint leaders with Essex and Lancashire.
A blistering 110 containing four fours and seven sixes in 96 balls from back-to-form John Morris failed to save Durham from a third league defeat and a second in as many days at the hands of Essex.
Morris and his team mates had reckoned without Essex's latest Law _ Danny, rather than Stuart this time helping to win the game with 82 to rescue the hosts from 91 for five.
But it took ninth-wicket pair Mark Ilott and Ashley Cowan to see Essex past Durham's 208 for eight with an unbroken stand of 25.

Leicestershire confirmed their superiority over Hampshire with a 38-run win at Southampton, their 231 for six built around half-centuries from South African Neil Johnson (54) and Ben Smith (51 not out).
Lancashire's ex-England batsman Jason Gallian made an unbeaten 54 to steer his county to a narrow victory over Nottinghamshire at Old Trafford.
Middlesex were led by captain Mike Gatting's 82 as they edged past Derbyshire's 178 all out with just one ball to spare.

Five individual innings between 20 and 40 saw Warwickshire to a four-wicket win at Edgbaston over Yorkshire, whose batting efforts were hampered by a four-wicket mid-innings burst from South African paceman Allan Donald.
